Container.name: Container
Container.Description: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.)  A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.FieldDescription: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element.  For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object.   The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character.   This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used.  DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

fields.name: PrevWorkflow
fields.FieldDescription:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition. 

A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation.  Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

fields.name: Workstation
fields.FieldDescription:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

fields.FieldDescription:
Resource where this Container is currently being processed (or will be processed). By default, this is the Resource that will receive the Production (throughput) credit for processing this Container.

Move-in sets this field to the Resource that is (will be) doing the work. By default that is the Resource that is used for Completion and Move-out transactions.

The Resource specified here is the Resource that will show this Container in its list of current Containers.

fields.FieldDescription: A Spec Status is used to manage the status of a Container for the duration of processing against its current Spec. fields.name: SplitFrom
fields.FieldDescription: Reference to the Container from which this Container was created. This will only have a value if this Container was created by a Split-type transaction.

fields.name: StartReason
fields.FieldDescription: Reference to the Start Reason (Code) for this Container. Start reasons are primarily used for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history). WIP Messages can also be defined for an Start Reason Code, which means they apply to all Containers with that Start Reason.

fields.name: Status
fields.FieldDescription:
Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. 
Valid values and their meanings are:
0 = Deleted
1 = Active
2 = Closed
3 = In Transit (shipped)
4 = Issued (component)
A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

fields.name: ThisContainerLost

A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.
